summary.es: Un amigo le transmite el mensaje de recuperación y llega a su primera reunión a los 16 años, pero se niega a aceptar su problema con la bebida. title.en: Alberto - The Decision
title.es: Alberto - La decisión

summary.en: Resented to his parents for his abandonment and consumed by his fears and insecurities, Alberto resorted to alcohol to face his fears and to be courageous. In a moment of clarity, seeing your child in danger, makes the decision to stop drinking and arrives at AA. Photo Credit: Becki W.
summary.es: Resentido con sus padres por su abandono y consumido por sus miedos e inseguridades, Alberto recurre al alcohol para enfrentar sus temores y darse valor. En un momento de claridad, viendo a su hijo en peligro, toma la decisión de dejar de beber y llega a AA. Photo Credit: Becki W.

items.summary: Se casó a los doce años con la botella, y desde entonces, Anselmo vivía una vida de egoísmo y resentimientos, haciendo lo que fuera necesario con tal de conseguir alcohol. El alcohol se convierte en su enemigo hasta que se entrega por completo al programa de Alcohólicos Anónimos. Photo Credit: Jeanna T.

title.en: Anselmo M. - My best friend
title.es: Anselmo M. - Mi mejor amigo

summary.en: He married at the age of twelve with the bottle, and since then, Anselmo lived a life of selfishness and resentment, doing whatever was necessary to get alcohol. Alcohol becomes your enemy until it is delivered completely to the Alcoholics Anonymous program. Photo Credit: Jeanna T.

Photo Credit: A. Murphy

title.en: Edgar M. - A new life
title.es: Edgar M. - Una nueva vida

summary.en: In the face of the threat of his wife to abandon him if he does not stop drinking, Edgar decides to go to Alcoholics Anonymous, and there, together with his wife who becomes his support, he begins the path of the sobriety. Now, the most important thing for him is to pass the message to another alcoholic. Photo Credit: Becki W.
summary.es: Ante la amenaza de su esposa de abandonarlo si no deja de beber, Edgar decide ir a Alcohólicos Anónimos, y ahí, junto a su esposa que se convierte en su apoyo, comienza el camino de la sobriedad. Ahora, lo más importante para él es: pasar el mensaje a otro alcohólico. Photo Credit: Becki W.

items.title: Elmer D. - El mensajero
items.summary: Descripción: Para Elmer una vida sin alcohol era inimaginable, bebía sin parar y termina viviendo en la calle pidiendo dinero para comprar alcohol. Una “goma” moral lo hace recapacitar y su Poder Superior lo lleva a AA. Photo Credit: Carole B.

title.en: Elmer D. - The messenger
title.es: Elmer D. - El mensajero

summary.en: Description: For Elmer a life without alcohol was unimaginable, he drank without stopping and ends up living on the street asking for money to buy alcohol. A moral “goma” makes him retrain and his Higher Power takes him to AA. Photo Credit: Carole B.
summary.es: Descripción: Para Elmer una vida sin alcohol era inimaginable, bebía sin parar y termina viviendo en la calle pidiendo dinero para comprar alcohol. Una “goma” moral lo hace recapacitar y su Poder Superior lo lleva a AA. Photo Credit: Carole B.

items.title: Eloy E. - De la oscuridad a la luz
items.summary: Dominado por los resentimientos, Eloy descubre el alcohol a los 13 años y con ello una sensación de paz, alegría y tranquilidad. Con esa sensación se despertó el diablillo que llevaba adentro, al que llamaba “resentimiento hacia mi padre”. En el programa se libera de ese resentimiento, que era la barrera a su recuperación, y su padre se convierte en su mejor amigo. Photo Credit: Eric S.

title.en: Eloy E. - From darkness to light
title.es: Eloy E. - De la oscuridad a la luz

summary.en: Dominated by the resentments, Eloy discovers alcohol at the age of 13 and with it a sense of peace, joy and tranquility. With that feeling, the devil inside was awakened, who was called “resentment to my father.” In the program it is released from that resentment, which was the barrier to his recovery, and his father becomes his best friend. Photo Credit: Eric S.
summary.es: Dominado por los resentimientos, Eloy descubre el alcohol a los 13 años y con ello una sensación de paz, alegría y tranquilidad. Con esa sensación se despertó el diablillo que llevaba adentro, al que llamaba “resentimiento hacia mi padre”. En el programa se libera de ese resentimiento, que era la barrera a su recuperación, y su padre se convierte en su mejor amigo. Photo Credit: Eric S.

items.title: Hugo L. - Milagros
items.summary: Descripción: Comienza a beber desde muy temprana edad y desde la primera vez no pudo, ni quiso parar. Vive una vida ingobernable hasta que llega a AA impulsado por un gran miedo a lo que le podría pasar si continuaba bebiendo así. Dios y AA hacen milagros y Hugo logra mantenerse sobrio un día a la vez. Photo Credit: Michael C.

title.en: Hugo L. - Miracles
title.es: Hugo L. - Milagros

summary.en: Description: Start drinking from a very early age and from the first time he couldn't, nor wanted to stop. He lives an ungovernable life until he arrives at AA driven by a great fear of what could happen to him if he continued to drink like this. God and AA do miracles and Hugo manages to stay sober One Day at a Time. Photo Credit: Michael C.
summary.es: Descripción: Comienza a beber desde muy temprana edad y desde la primera vez no pudo, ni quiso parar. Vive una vida ingobernable hasta que llega a AA impulsado por un gran miedo a lo que le podría pasar si continuaba bebiendo así. Dios y AA hacen milagros y Hugo logra mantenerse sobrio un día a la vez. Photo Credit: Michael C.

items.title: José C. - Mi infancia, mi alcoholismo y mi recuperación
items.summary: José descubre el alcohol y de ser un estudiante con aspiraciones se convierte en un borracho sin esperanzas. Pierde a su familia y su alcoholismo convierte su sueño americano en una pesadilla. Photo Credit: R. Hamm

title.en: José C. - My childhood, my alcoholism and my recovery
title.es: José C. - Mi infancia, mi alcoholismo y mi recuperación

summary.en: Joseph discovers alcohol and being a student with aspirations becomes a hopeless drunk. Losing your family and your alcoholism makes your American dream a nightmare. Photo Credit: R. Hamm
summary.es: José descubre el alcohol y de ser un estudiante con aspiraciones se convierte en un borracho sin esperanzas. Pierde a su familia y su alcoholismo convierte su sueño americano en una pesadilla. Photo Credit: R. Hamm

items.title: Manuel R. - El privilegio
items.summary: Borracho todos los días y hasta durmiendo en los parques, Manuel se convierte en una persona indeseable dentro de la sociedad; creía que su destino era morir borracho, pero su Poder Superior tenía otros planes para él, y le regala el privilegio de llevar el mensaje a otros alcohólicos. Photo Credit: Drew S.

title.en: Manuel R. - Privilege
title.es: Manuel R. - El privilegio

summary.en: Drunk every day and even sleeping in the parks, Manuel becomes an undesirable person within society; he believed his destiny was to die drunk, but his Higher Power had other plans for him, and gives him the privilege of bringing the message to other alcoholics. Photo Credit: Drew S.
summary.es: Borracho todos los días y hasta durmiendo en los parques, Manuel se convierte en una persona indeseable dentro de la sociedad; creía que su destino era morir borracho, pero su Poder Superior tenía otros planes para él, y le regala el privilegio de llevar el mensaje a otros alcohólicos. Photo Credit: Drew S.

items.title: Cal “We’ve been dancing together ever since.”
items.summary: When they were drinking, Cal and his wife loved to dance—but they were dance partners in the disease of alcoholism. Photo Credit: A. Conway

title.en: Cal “We’ve been dancing together ever since.”
title.es: Cal “Hemos estado bailando juntos desde entonces”.

summary.en: When they were drinking, Cal and his wife loved to dance—but they were dance partners in the disease of alcoholism. Photo Credit: A. Conway
summary.es: Cuando bebían, Cal y su esposa amaban bailar, pero eran compañeros de baile en la enfermedad del alcoholismo. Crédito fotográfico: A. Conway

items.title: Emma A. “I’ve been coming to Step One as far back as I can remember.”
items.summary: She grew up feeling distant from friends and family, isolated both by alcoholism and her then-hidden identity as a trans woman. Finally, in a moment of clarity, she understood that “to survive I had to put down the drink.” Photo Credit: A. Conway

title.en: Emma A. “I’ve been coming to Step One as far back as I can remember.”
title.es: Emma A. “He estado viniendo a Paso Uno tan lejos como puedo recordar.”

summary.en: She grew up feeling distant from friends and family, isolated both by alcoholism and her then-hidden identity as a trans woman. Finally, in a moment of clarity, she understood that “to survive I had to put down the drink.” Photo Credit: A. Conway
summary.es: Se sentía distante de los amigos y la familia, aislada tanto por el alcoholismo como por su identidad entonces oculta como una mujer trans. Finalmente, en un momento de claridad, entendió que “para sobrevivir tenía que bajar la bebida”. Crédito fotográfico: A. Conway

items.title: Jim T. “Finally, I really was sick and tired.”
items.summary: Jim came into AA, but kept on drinking between meetings. He watched his family began to fall apart and he saw that he might lose everything unless he became honest with himself and others. Photo Credit: J. Graham

title.en: Jim T. “Finally, I really was sick and tired.”
title.es: Jim T. “Finalmente, realmente estaba enfermo y cansado”.

summary.en: Jim came into AA, but kept on drinking between meetings. He watched his family began to fall apart and he saw that he might lose everything unless he became honest with himself and others. Photo Credit: J. Graham
summary.es: Jim entró en AA, pero siguió bebiendo entre las reuniones. Vio que su familia empezó a desmoronarse y vio que podía perder todo a menos que se hiciera honesto con él y con otros. Crédito fotográfico: J. Graham

items.title: Jody “I had no doubt that I was exactly where I was supposed to be.”
items.summary: Forty-one felonies later, she ended up in prison where a chance remark during an AA meeting led her to a spiritual experience. Photo Credit: B.Willman

title.en: Jody “I had no doubt that I was exactly where I was supposed to be.”
title.es: Jody “No tenía ninguna duda de que estaba exactamente donde debía estar.”

summary.en: Forty-one felonies later, she ended up in prison where a chance remark during an AA meeting led her to a spiritual experience. Photo Credit: B.Willman
summary.es: Cuarenta y uno de los delincuentes más tarde, terminó en prisión donde una observación casual durante una reunión de AA la llevó a una experiencia espiritual. Crédito fotográfico: B.Willman

items.title: Linda-Ann “I knew my Dad would love AA.”
items.summary: She was told to focus on her own recovery, not her father’s—but through a variety of strategies, she helped him to enjoy long-term sobriety. Photo Credit: Joe L.

title.en: Linda-Ann “I knew my Dad would love AA.”
title.es: Linda-Ann “Sabía que a mi papá le encantaría AA”.

summary.en: She was told to focus on her own recovery, not her father’s—but through a variety of strategies, she helped him to enjoy long-term sobriety. Photo Credit: Joe L.
summary.es: Se le dijo que se centrara en su propia recuperación, no en la de su padre, pero a través de una variedad de estrategias, ella le ayudó a disfrutar de sobriedad a largo plazo. Crédito por foto: Joe L.

items.title: Liz “Nobody really cared. They were just happy to see me.”
items.summary: During her first 90 days after a relapse she was flying solo—“mistake number one”—before the women in her group gathered around her. Photo Credit: C. Tremblay

title.en: Liz “Nobody really cared. They were just happy to see me.”
title.es: Liz “A nadie le importaba mucho. Estaban felices de verme.

summary.en: During her first 90 days after a relapse she was flying solo—“mistake number one”—before the women in her group gathered around her. Photo Credit: C. Tremblay
summary.es: Durante sus primeros 90 días después de una recaída ella volaba solo —“el primer golpe”— antes de que las mujeres de su grupo se reunieran alrededor de ella. Crédito fotográfico: C. Tremblay

items.title: Rodney W. “A messenger to save the lives of others.”
items.summary: His mother took out an insurance policy on him because she didn’t think he would live until the age of 30. While drinking, he dreamed of “a better place” away from pain and despair. That place, it turned out, was AA. Photo Credit: C. Tremblay

title.en: Rodney W. “A messenger to save the lives of others.”
title.es: Rodney W. “Un mensajero para salvar las vidas de los demás”.

summary.en: His mother took out an insurance policy on him because she didn’t think he would live until the age of 30. While drinking, he dreamed of “a better place” away from pain and despair. That place, it turned out, was AA. Photo Credit: C. Tremblay
summary.es: Su madre le sacó una póliza de seguro porque no pensaba que viviría hasta los 30 años. Mientras bebía, soñaba con “un lugar mejor” lejos del dolor y la desesperación. Ese lugar, resultó ser AA. Crédito fotográfico: C. Tremblay

items.title: Sandy “There is nothing more important in my life than Alcoholics Anonymous”
items.summary: From an upper middle class family to detox and the Salvation Army, she found her way to a new life and a happy retirement by doing “all the things that AA teaches us to do.” Photo Credit: M. Tipper

title.en: Sandy “There is nothing more important in my life than Alcoholics Anonymous”
title.es: Sandy “No hay nada más importante en mi vida que Alcohólicos Anónimos”

summary.en: From an upper middle class family to detox and the Salvation Army, she found her way to a new life and a happy retirement by doing “all the things that AA teaches us to do.” Photo Credit: M. Tipper
summary.es: De una familia de clase media alta a la desintoxicación y el Ejército de Salvación, encontró su camino a una nueva vida y una feliz jubilación haciendo “todas las cosas que AA nos enseña a hacer”. Crédito de la foto: M. Tipper

items.title: Sky “I grew up in A.A.”
items.summary: The child of a sober, but mentally ill, mother, Sky went to meetings for most of her childhood, but then drug use in high school turned into heavy drinking. AA helped her get sober, but she truly found “her people” went to her first YPAA conference.

AA la ayudó a ponerse sobria, pero realmente encontró que “su gente” fue a su primera conferencia de YPAA.

items.title: Eleanor F. “Hope was around the corner.”
items.summary: It got so bad Eleanor nearly made a pact with the devil to keep from drinking—but at the last minute, she joined AA. Forty years later, she goes to meetings, sponsors other women, speaks at AA events and does service. Her message: “Don’t give up hope. It is always there for us.”

playlists: Voices of Women: “We need to give ourselves time.”

summary.es: Se puso tan mal que Eleanor casi hizo un pacto con el diablo para no beber, pero en el último momento, se unió a AA. This realization brought effected a true transformation in their relationship. Photocredit: K. Cook

summary.en: With decades of strong sobriety, Scott decided he wanted to get close to his ill and aging father, who had kept him at arm’s length throughout their lives. Yet he could never crack the barrier, until his sponsor suggested that Scott needed to change, because his father was unlikely to. This realization brought effected a true transformation in their relationship. Photocredit: K. Cook
summary.es: Con décadas de fuerte sobriedad, Scott decidió que quería acercarse a su padre enfermo y envejecido, que lo había mantenido a lo largo de sus vidas. Sin embargo, nunca pudo romper la barrera, hasta que su padrino sugirió que Scott necesitaba cambiar, porque su padre era poco probable. Esta realización produjo una verdadera transformación en su relación. Photocredit: K. Cook

items.title: Ken M. “Forget everything you thought you knew.”
items.summary: When Ken took his first drink after a tough childhood and a motorcycle accident at the age of 18, he found an illusory freedom and happiness. Twenty years later, cycling in and out of A.A., he met a sponsor who advised him that his old way of thinking was keeping him drunk. Photocredit: B.Willman

summary.es: Cuando Ken tomó su primera bebida después de una infancia dura y un accidente de motocicleta a los 18 años, encontró una libertad ilusoria y felicidad. Veinte años después, ciclándose dentro y fuera de A.A., conoció a un padrino que le aconsejó que su vieja forma de pensar lo mantenía borracho. Fotocrédito: B.Willman

items.title: Byron B. “The solution wasn’t me.” - AA Grapevine
items.summary: “They didn’t say keep coming back. They said don’t come back.” One Thanksgiving, Byron found himself completely alone—rejected by his family, even his church group, because of the trail of devastation his drinking had left behind. His sponsor told him to let go of pride and let the program in. Photocredit: K. Cook

playlists: Sponsorship: “Willing to go to any length.”

summary.es: “No dijeron que siguieran regresando. Dijeron que no regreses. Un Día de Acción de Gracias, Byron se encontró completamente solo—rechazado por su familia, incluso su grupo de la iglesia, debido al rastro de devastación que su bebida había dejado atrás. Su padrino le dijo que dejara ir de orgullo y dejara entrar el programa. Photocredit: K. Cook

items.title: Kathy R. “I was surrounded.”
items.summary: Kathy’s idea of intimacy was: “Come here, come here, go away, go away.” But when she walked into her first meeting she was surrounded by sober women—and decided she wanted what they had. These women included her sponsor who helped Kathy with what she most needed: the Steps. Photo Credit: S. Driedger

playlists: Sponsorship: “Willing to go to any length.”

summary.es: La idea de Kathy de intimidad era: “Ven aquí, ven aquí, vete, vete”. Pero cuando entró en su primera reunión estaba rodeada de mujeres sobrias, y decidió que quería lo que tenían. Estas mujeres incluyeron su padrino que ayudó a Kathy con lo que más necesitaba: los pasos. Crédito fotográfico: S. Driedger

items.title: PS. W. “Not my business.”
items.summary: Going to meetings and continuing to drink? PS describes it as an “awful crossroads in my life,” but finally understood that willpower wasn’t the answer. She called her sponsor about every drink trigger, from traffic jams to not getting her way at home. There was a simple phrase her sponsor repeated that got her through those first, tough 90 days. Photo Credit: J. Thacker

playlists: Sponsorship: “Willing to go to any length.”

title.en: PS. W. “Not my business.”
title.es: PS. W. “No es asunto mío”.

summary.en: Going to meetings and continuing to drink? PS describes it as an “awful crossroads in my life,” but finally understood that willpower wasn’t the answer. She called her sponsor about every drink trigger, from traffic jams to not getting her way at home. There was a simple phrase her sponsor repeated that got her through those first, tough 90 days. Photo Credit: J. Thacker
summary.es: ¿Ir a las reuniones y seguir bebiendo? PS lo describe como una “crucijada viciosa en mi vida”, pero finalmente entendió que el poder de voluntad no era la respuesta. La llamó padrino sobre cada gatillo de bebida, desde las mermeladas de tráfico para no conseguir su camino en casa. Hubo una frase sencilla que su padrino repitió que la hizo pasar por esos primeros, duros 90 días. Crédito fotográfico: J. Thacker

items.title: Myra G. “Whatever you do, be honest.” - AA Grapevine
items.summary: Thirty days into sobriety, Myra got an interview for her dream job. One problem: her DWI arrest, two years before. She was sure she needed to lie to get the job, but before the interview she decided to ask her sponsor for advice. It was a good thing she did. Photo Credit: J. Thacker

playlists: Sponsorship: “Willing to go to any length.”

title.es: Myra G. “Hagas lo que hagas, sé honesta”. - AA Grapevine

summary.en: Thirty days into sobriety, Myra got an interview for her dream job. One problem: her DWI arrest, two years before. She was sure she needed to lie to get the job, but before the interview she decided to ask her sponsor for advice. It was a good thing she did. Photo Credit: J. Thacker
summary.es: Treinta días en sobriedad, Myra consiguió una entrevista para su trabajo de ensueño. Un problema: la detención de su agente, dos años antes. Estaba segura de que necesitaba mentir para conseguir el trabajo, pero antes de la entrevista decidió pedirle consejo a padrino. Fue algo bueno lo que hizo. Crédito fotográfico: J. Thacker
